## Physics

How things move, collide and stay together.

## Math

The math behind motion: change over time, rotations, numbers on a computer.

| | Concept | In short | Part of | First cited in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ○ | Barycentric coordinates | A point described as a mix of the corners around it, with weights that sum to 1, like the interpolation of varyings in a fragment shader |  | [Advanced Character Physics](https://edelkas.github.io/n/files/bib/jakobsen.pdf) |
| ○ | Complexity, O(N) | How the work grows with the number of objects: O(N) doubles when they double, O(N²) becomes four times |  | [Data structures and algorithms for contact detection in numerical simulation of discrete particle systems](https://www2.msm.ctw.utwente.nl/sluding/PAPERS/OgarkoWCPT2010.pdf) |
| ○ | Conjugate gradient | A way to solve a big system of equations in rounds, where each round avoids undoing the ones before |  | [Advanced Character Physics](https://edelkas.github.io/n/files/bib/jakobsen.pdf) |
| ○ | Delaunay triangulation | Joining points into triangles, or tetrahedra, so that near ones are joined: contacts are then looked for only along the edges. Weighted, it takes the radii into account; flipping updates it when points move |  | [Data structures and algorithms for contact detection in numerical simulation of discrete particle systems](https://www2.msm.ctw.utwente.nl/sluding/PAPERS/OgarkoWCPT2010.pdf) |
| ◐ | Derivative | How fast a quantity changes at an instant: velocity is the derivative of position, acceleration that of velocity |  | [004](../logbook/004-the-detour.md) |
| ◐ | Floating point precision | Numbers on a computer have a limited number of digits: 32-bit floats are fast on the GPU, but rounding errors add up |  | [004](../logbook/004-the-detour.md) |
| ◐ | Integral | The reverse of a derivative: adding up small changes over time, such as velocity into position |  | [004](../logbook/004-the-detour.md) |
| ◐ | Jacobian | The table of how much each rule changes when each coordinate moves: it gives the directions a solver pushes along |  | [Advanced Character Physics](https://edelkas.github.io/n/files/bib/jakobsen.pdf) |
| ○ | Linear complementarity problem | The math name of the contact problem: each contact either pushes or is separating, never both |  | [Iterative Dynamics with Temporal Coherence](https://box2d.org/files/ErinCatto_IterativeDynamics_GDC2005.pdf) |
| ○ | Mass matrix | The masses and inertias of all bodies in one table, so the equations of every body can be written at once |  | [Iterative Dynamics with Temporal Coherence](https://box2d.org/files/ErinCatto_IterativeDynamics_GDC2005.pdf) |
| ◐ | Newton-Raphson method | Improving a guess step by step: for a square root, average the guess with the number divided by the guess |  | [Advanced Character Physics](https://edelkas.github.io/n/files/bib/jakobsen.pdf) |
| ○ | Robust geometric tests | Tests such as "which side of this triangle is the point on" that rounding errors can answer wrongly, and the exact or interval arithmetic used to trust them |  | [Data structures and algorithms for contact detection in numerical simulation of discrete particle systems](https://www2.msm.ctw.utwente.nl/sluding/PAPERS/OgarkoWCPT2010.pdf) |
| ◐ | Rotation invariance | Turning the whole scene must give the same motion, only turned: a rule that treats x, y and z one by one breaks it, like a Box3 that changes size when the mesh turns |  | [026](../logbook/026-the-marble-in-the-pocket.md) |
| ○ | Taylor expansion | Replacing a curve, near a point where you know it, with something simpler: at first order, its tangent line |  | [Advanced Character Physics](https://edelkas.github.io/n/files/bib/jakobsen.pdf) |

## GPU

WebGPU, WGSL and how to make thousands of threads work.

| | Concept | In short | Part of | First cited in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ○ | Abstract numeric types | The types of numbers written without a suffix (AbstractInt, AbstractFloat): they adapt to i32, u32 or f32 where they are used, which the spec calls concretization | WGSL | [WGSL specification, §7.2 Value Declarations](https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/#value-decls) |
| ○ | Access mode | Whether a variable's memory can be read, written or both. Only storage buffers let you choose, and they are read-only unless you write read_write | var declaration | [WGSL specification, §7.3 var Declarations](https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/#var-decls) |
| ● | **[Adapter and device](../guides/adapter-and-device.md)** | How a page gets the GPU: the adapter stands for a GPU on the system, the device is our own connection to it | WebGPU | [guides index](../guides/README.md) |
| ○ | Address space | Where a variable's memory lives, written var<…>: function, private, workgroup, uniform, storage, immediate, or handle for textures and samplers | var declaration | [WGSL specification, §7.3 var Declarations](https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/#var-decls) |
| ● | **[Async pipeline creation](../guides/pipeline-creation.md)** | createComputePipelineAsync() returns a promise that resolves when the pipeline is compiled. It is not faster: it lets the rest of the GPU work go on meanwhile, and a mistake rejects the promise with a GPUPipelineError | Compute pipeline | [pipelines](../guides/pipelines.md) |
| ● | **[Atomic operations](../guides/atomics.md)** | Memory updates that stay correct even when thousands of threads write to the same place: in WGSL, atomicAdd() adds to an integer and returns the value from before, in one move that cannot be cut in two |  | [004](../logbook/004-the-detour.md) |
| ○ | Barriers | workgroupBarrier(), storageBarrier() and textureBarrier(): a line in a compute shader that the threads of a workgroup cross together, so that what any of them wrote before it is visible to all of them after it | Workgroups and dispatch | [dispatch-and-workgroups](../guides/dispatch-and-workgroups.md) |
| ◐ | Billboard | A flat shape turned to face the camera in every frame, the base of most impostors | Impostor | [009](../logbook/009-the-first-picture.md) |
| ● | **[Bind group](../guides/bind-groups.md)** | A fixed list that puts a real buffer in each numbered slot of one group of a shader. Made once, set before the shader runs: the pipeline is which program, the bind group is which data | WebGPU | [guides index](../guides/README.md) |
| ◐ | Bind group layout | The description of the slots of one bind group: for each binding, what kind of resource goes there and which shader stages see it. Made by hand with createBindGroupLayout(), or taken from a pipeline | Bind group | [pipelines](../guides/pipelines.md) |
| ○ | Blelloch scan | A prefix sum that adds pairs up like a tournament and then comes back down: few rounds, and about twice the additions of a plain walk | Prefix sum (scan) | [Parallel Prefix Sum (Scan) with CUDA](https://developer.nvidia.com/gpugems/gpugems3/part-vi-gpu-computing/chapter-39-parallel-prefix-sum-scan-cuda) |
| ● | **[Buffer](../guides/buffers.md)** | A block of GPU memory holding raw bytes, declared up front with everything it will be used for | WebGPU | [guides index](../guides/README.md) |
| ● | **[Buffer mapping](../guides/readback.md)** | mapAsync() opens a buffer to JavaScript and unmap() gives it back to the GPU: while it is mapped, no GPU command can use it | Readback | [buffers](../guides/buffers.md) |
| ○ | Commands and queue | GPU work is recorded first, and runs only when it is submitted to the queue | WebGPU | [guides index](../guides/README.md) |
| ○ | Compatibility mode | A restricted WebGPU that also runs on older graphics APIs, such as OpenGL ES 3.1 | WebGPU | [004](../logbook/004-the-detour.md) |

| ◐ | Conservative depth | A promise that the depth a shader writes is only farther, or only nearer, than its triangle, so the early depth test can still run: @builtin(frag_depth, greater) in WGSL | Early depth test | [046](../logbook/046-a-promise-not-yet-kept.md) |

| ○ | Const-expression | An expression the compiler can evaluate while compiling the shader, such as 2 * 3 or vec3(1, 2, 3) | WGSL | [WGSL specification, §7.2 Value Declarations](https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/#value-decls) |
| ◐ | Constraint graph coloring | Splitting constraints into groups that share no body, so each group can be solved in parallel |  | [004](../logbook/004-the-detour.md) |
| ○ | Constructible type | A type whose values can be created, copied and passed around: scalars, vectors, matrices, fixed-size arrays and structs made of them | WGSL | [WGSL specification, §7.2 Value Declarations](https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/#value-decls) |
| ◐ | Counting sort | Sorting by a small key without comparing: count how many have each key, sum the counts to find where each key's part begins, then drop every item into its part |  | [036](../logbook/036-the-address-book.md) |
| ◐ | Deferred shading | Drawing first only what each pixel shows (depth, normal, color), then working out the light once per pixel |  | [046](../logbook/046-a-promise-not-yet-kept.md) |
| ○ | Depth pre-pass | A cheap first drawing that fills only the depth, so the costly one can skip what is hidden |  | [046](../logbook/046-a-promise-not-yet-kept.md) |

| ◐ | Device loss | The browser can take the GPU back at any time: every buffer and pipeline, and the data in them, must then be created again | Adapter and device | [adapter-and-device](../guides/adapter-and-device.md) |

| ◐ | Early depth test | The GPU compares a pixel with what is already drawn before running its shader, and skips the hidden ones for free |  | [046](../logbook/046-a-promise-not-yet-kept.md) |
| ◐ | Entry point | The function where a shader starts, marked @compute, @vertex or @fragment. A pipeline compiles only the code its entry point reaches: the rest of the module is dropped | WGSL | [WGSL specification, §2.1 Shader Lifecycle](https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/#shader-lifecycle) |
| ○ | Error scope | Catches WebGPU errors in code: push a scope before the calls, pop it after to get the first error, or null | WebGPU errors | [buffers](../guides/buffers.md) |
| ◐ | First-fit coloring | Giving each constraint the first group where both its bodies are free. Simple and kept from step to step, but it uses more groups than the minimum, and a body in more constraints than there are groups leaves some out | Constraint graph coloring | [Box2D, constraint_graph.c](https://github.com/erincatto/box2d/blob/main/src/constraint_graph.c) |
| ◐ | Forward shading | Working out the light in each shape's own shader as it is drawn, hidden pixels included |  | [047](../logbook/047-once-per-pixel.md) |
| ○ | GPU-resident simulation | Keeping the simulation's data on the GPU, and not reading it back every frame |  | [004](../logbook/004-the-detour.md) |

| ◐ | Hillis and Steele scan | A prefix sum in few rounds: every element adds the one 1 place to its left, then 2 places, then 4. | ○ | let declaration | A name for a value computed while the shader runs and fixed from then on: only inside functions, and it can also hold a pointer | Value declaration | [WGSL specification, §7.2 Value Declarations](https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/#value-decls) |

## Engine design

How an engine is organized, measured and scaled across devices.

| | Concept | In short | Part of | First cited in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ○ | Benchmark scenes | Standard test scenes, such as a stack of boxes or a dam break, to compare algorithms fairly |  | [004](../logbook/004-the-detour.md) |
| ○ | Determinism | Two runs from the same start give exactly the same numbers. On the GPU, threads adding floats to the same body in a different order each run can break it |  | [010](../logbook/010-the-ground.md) |
| ○ | Entity component system (ECS) | Organizing a game as plain data components processed by systems, instead of objects with methods |  | [004](../logbook/004-the-detour.md) |
| ○ | Frame budget | The slice of each frame the physics may use, for example 2 to 4 ms of the 16.7 ms available at 60 FPS |  | [004](../logbook/004-the-detour.md) |
| ○ | Job system | Splitting the work of a step into small jobs spread over the CPU cores |  | [004](../logbook/004-the-detour.md) |
| ◐ | Particle properties in one buffer | What a particle is and does not change in a step, four numbers each in one buffer, the radius first: one of a shader's 8 storage buffers for all of them |  | [049](../logbook/049-a-radius-each.md) |
| ◐ | Quality tiers | The same simulation at different costs: fewer particles, substeps and solver rounds on weaker devices |  | [004](../logbook/004-the-detour.md) |
| ◐ | The precision of a page's clock | Browsers round the clocks a page can read, so they cannot be used to spy: performance.now() moved in steps of 0.1 ms in Chrome on our Mac and of 1 ms on an iPhone. Averaging many runs still measures below the step |  | [020](../logbook/020-a-cheap-launch.md) |
| ○ | Thermal throttling | Phones slow down as they heat up, so speed must be measured over minutes, not seconds |  | [004](../logbook/004-the-detour.md) |
